issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a parameterless method getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns an int (total number of students). The solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) with a boolean parameter, changing the method signature. This parameter mismatch will confuse students about which method to implement and will prevent tests or instructor-provided code expecting the no-argument method from compiling or running against the solution implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the specification by changing the solution method signature to public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() (no parameters) that returns numberOfInscribedStudents + numberOfGuestStudents. Update calls in the solution (e.g., getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents) to use the no-arg method. Alternatively, if a parameterized behavior is desired, update the problem statement and template to document and require getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) instead, but prefer the no-arg version to match the UML and task description.

issues.description: The UML and problem description specify a method getTotalNumberOfStudents() with no parameters that returns the total number of students. The solution implementation instead defines getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) (a different signature), changing the API for the same conceptual operation. This divergence between the stated requirement (no-arg method) and the solution's method signature creates confusion for students mapping the task to the implementation and will break expectation-based tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the solution to implement the no-argument method public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns numberOfInscribedStudents + numberOfGuestStudents. Remove the boolean parameter and update all internal calls (e.g., getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents() and getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor()) to call the no-arg method so the implementation matches the UML and problem description.
